tasks.description: Connect the frontend and backend for the problem library to enable data flow.

tasks.description: Create the backend logic for users to submit code and store submissions.

tasks.name: Build Code Evaluation System
tasks.description: Implement a system to evaluate submitted code against test cases.

tasks.description: Create the frontend interface for user profiles, including stats and achievements.

tasks.name: Implement User Profiles Backend
tasks.description: Develop the backend to manage user data and profile information.

tasks.name: Create Leaderboard UI
tasks.description: Design the frontend for displaying user rankings and scores.

tasks.name: Develop Leaderboard Backend
tasks.description: Implement the backend logic to calculate and retrieve leaderboard data.

tasks.name: Add Hints and Explanations Feature
tasks.description: Develop the backend to store and retrieve hints and explanations for problems.

tasks.name: Test Problem Library Functionality
tasks.description: Perform testing to ensure the problem library works as expected.

tasks.name: Test Code Submission and Evaluation
tasks.description: Test the code submission and evaluation system for accuracy and reliability.

tasks.name: Test User Profiles
tasks.description: Ensure user profiles display correct data and function as intended.

tasks.name: Test Leaderboard
tasks.description: Verify the leaderboard displays accurate rankings and scores.

tasks.name: Deploy ACM Problem-Solving Platform
tasks.description: Deploy the platform to a production environment.

T1.implementation_approach: Use a component-based approach with frameworks like React or Angular to design an intuitive and responsive UI for the problem library.
T1.notes: Focus on user experience and accessibility.

T2.implementation_approach: Develop RESTful APIs to handle problem creation, retrieval, update, and deletion using a backend framework.

T3.implementation_approach: Design a normalized schema to store problem details, tags, difficulty levels, and metadata.
T3.notes: Optimize for query performance and scalability.

T4.implementation_approach: Connect the frontend and backend using API endpoints and ensure seamless data flow.
T4.notes: Handle errors and loading states effectively.

T5.implementation_approach: Develop a feature to allow users to submit code, store submissions, and track their status.
T5.notes: Ensure security and prevent code injection.

T6.implementation_approach: Build a sandboxed environment to execute and evaluate user-submitted code against test cases.

T7.implementation_approach: Design a user-friendly interface for displaying and editing user profiles.
T7.notes: Include features like profile picture upload and activity tracking.

T8.implementation_approach: Develop APIs to manage user profile data, including retrieval, update, and deletion.

T9.implementation_approach: Design a leaderboard interface to display rankings based on user performance.

T10.implementation_approach: Develop APIs to calculate and retrieve leaderboard data based on user submissions and scores.

T11.implementation_approach: Develop a feature to add hints and explanations for problems, accessible via the UI.

T12.implementation_approach: Write unit and integration tests to verify the functionality of the problem library.
T12.notes: Focus on edge cases and error handling.

T13.implementation_approach: Test the code submission and evaluation system using various test cases and scenarios.
T13.notes: Ensure security and performance under load.

T14.implementation_approach: Write tests to verify the functionality of user profiles, including data retrieval and updates.

T15.implementation_approach: Test the leaderboard functionality, including sorting, filtering, and real-time updates.

T16.implementation_approach: Deploy the platform using cloud services and CI/CD pipelines for automated deployment.

from flask_sqlalchemy import SQLAlchemy

# Initialize SQLAlchemy instance
db = SQLAlchemy()

def init_db(app):
    """
    Initialize the database with the Flask app.

    Args:
        app (Flask): The Flask application instance.
    """
    db.init_app(app)

    with app.app_context():
        # Create all tables in the database based on the defined models
        db.create_all()

from app.database import db

class Problem(db.Model):
    __tablename__ = 'problems'

    id = db.Column(db.Integer, primary_key=True)
    title = db.Column(db.String(255), nullable=False)
    description = db.Column(db.Text, nullable=False)
    difficulty = db.Column(db.String(50), nullable=False)
    created_at = db.Column(db.DateTime, default=db.func.current_timestamp())
    updated_at = db.Column(db.DateTime, default=db.func.current_timestamp(), onupdate=db.func.current_timestamp())

    def __repr__(self):
        return f"<Problem {self.title}>"

from app.database import db

class User(db.Model):
    __tablename__ = 'users'

    id = db.Column(db.Integer, primary_key=True)
    username = db.Column(db.String(80), unique=True, nullable=False)
    email = db.Column(db.String(120), unique=True, nullable=False)
    password_hash = db.Column(db.String(128), nullable=False)

    def __repr__(self):
        return f'<User {self.username}>'

    def set_password(self, password):
        # This method would typically hash the password
        # Placeholder for password hashing logic
        self.password_hash = password

    def check_password(self, password):
        # This method would typically verify the hashed password
        # Placeholder for password verification logic
        return self.password_hash == password

from app.database import db


class Solution(db.Model):
    __tablename__ = 'solutions'

    id = db.Column(db.Integer, primary_key=True, autoincrement=True)
    code = db.Column(db.Text, nullable=False)
    language = db.Column(db.String(50), nullable=False)
    result = db.Column(db.String(50))
    submission_time = db.Column(db.DateTime, default=db.func.now())
    user_id = db.Column(db.Integer, db.ForeignKey('users.id'), nullable=False)
    problem_id = db.Column(db.Integer, db.ForeignKey('problems.id'), nullable=False)

    user = db.relationship('User', back_populates='solutions')
    problem = db.relationship('Problem', back_populates='solutions')

    def __repr__(self):
        return f'<Solution id={self.id} user_id={self.user_id} problem_id={self.problem_id}>'

from app.controllers.problem_controller import problem_blueprint
from app.controllers.user_controller import user_blueprint
from app.controllers.solution_controller import solution_blueprint

def register_blueprints(app):
    """
    Register all blueprints to the Flask application instance.

    Args:
        app (Flask): The Flask application instance.
    """
    app.register_blueprint(problem_blueprint)
    app.register_blueprint(user_blueprint)
    app.register_blueprint(solution_blueprint)

from flask import Flask
from app.database import db
from app.routes import register_blueprints

def create_app():
    app = Flask(__name__)
    
    # Configure the app (you can replace this with actual configuration as needed)
    app.config['SQLALCHEMY_DATABASE_URI'] = 'sqlite:///acm_platform.db'
    app.config['SQLALCHEMY_TRACK_MODIFICATIONS'] = False
    
    # Initialize the database
    db.init_app(app)
    
    # Register routes
    register_blueprints(app)
    
    return app

# ACM Problem-Solving Platform

A website designed to help users solve ACM-style competitive programming problems.

## Features

- Problem Library: A comprehensive library of ACM-style problems categorized by difficulty and topic.
- Code Submission and Evaluation: Allows users to submit code solutions and receive instant feedback on correctness and performance.
- User Profiles: Enables users to create profiles to track their progress, solved problems, and rankings.
- Leaderboard: Displays rankings of users based on their problem-solving performance.
- Hints and Explanations: Provides optional hints and detailed explanations for problems to aid learning.

## Setup

```bash
pip install -r requirements.txt
python app.py
```

## Usage

Open http://localhost:5000 in your browser.
